answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 121 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The delta graph is validated at intake and the prism frontier is published, thus the ancestry of every answer is public, and nadir anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Every submission must name 5 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
